paragraphs: In the club hour, May read an email on the library computer. Leo and Lily sat next to her. The library was quiet, and the afternoon light came through the window. "Grace wrote to me," said May. "Her class made a snowman." "A snowman in Singapore?" asked Leo.

"Yes, they made it from cotton, and it is for the class window," said May. "Ms. Ong gave each child a small job," said May. "Twelve children worked on it for three days." "Did they finish it?" asked Lily. "Yes, they finished it on Friday," said May.

"Is there a photo?" asked Leo. "Wait," said May, "I have just opened it." A big photo appeared on the screen after a minute. The three children looked at it for a long time. "Look at the hat!" said Lily. "It is red, and it is very big." "The scarf is blue," said Leo. "The eyes are two black buttons." "The snowman is about one meter tall," said May. "Which girl is Grace?" asked Lily. "She has two long braids and a yellow T-shirt," said May. "And the nose is orange," said May. Grace wrote, "It is a paper carrot."

"This is amazing," said Lily. "I am so excited about our reply." "What do we write?" asked Leo. "First, we say thank you for the photo," said May. "Then we ask about the snow," said Lily. "Is the cotton cold?" asked Leo with a smile. May laughed and said, "I cannot spell the word 'cotton'."

"Let's use the dictionary," said Lily. She took a green dictionary from the shelf. "Since you are the writer, you can type," said Leo. May looked at the letters in the dictionary and typed the word. "Now it is right," she said. Lily read the email once more and smiled at the photo. "Please tell Ms. Ong," wrote May, "that we love the snowman."
